title: Deployment watchdog: VPC API readiness, model warmup, and smoke verification suite
creator: Avery Lin
description:
Goal: implement a lightweight, robust post-deployment watchdog that runs immediately after a VPC/private deployment and validates: (1) API readiness (control plane + runtime endpoints), (2) model load and warmup for pinned model versions, and (3) a short smoke generation and end-to-end latency check. This ticket covers the orchestration harness, IaC hooks (Terraform module hooks/callbacks), and the set of smoke and load-lite tests that run as part of the post-deploy pipeline.

Scope:
- Add a reusable "watchdog" job that can be invoked by the Terraform deployment runner (via remote-exec or cloud build trigger) or by our deployment orchestrator.
- Implement API readiness probes that exercise the control-plane API (token auth, route config) and runtime inference endpoints (health + /v1/generate sample).
- Implement a model warmup flow that attempts model load, verifies KV cache population for a short prompt, and validates output tokens under latency thresholds.
- Smoke verification: a short deterministic prompt suite (3 prompts) to check semantics, structured output parsing, and function-calling sanity.
- Failure handling: clear error categories (config, network, model load, auth), automatic retry policy, and escalation actions (rollback suggestion + alert to on-call).
- Observability: emit metrics to Prometheus/Grafana dashboard and log structured events to the centralized audit log (for Private customers we write to customer log sink + internal incident logs).
- Deliverables: watchdog binary/script, Terraform module changes (callback hook docs), CI pipeline job, PR with tests, and a small runbook for SRE/solutions-eng.

Non-goals: deep performance load testing (separate load campaign job), long-duration warmups for very large models (>8B) — we provide fast checks only.
acceptance_criteria: Watchdog can be invoked from the Terraform deploy pipeline and returns an exit code that reflects health (0=ok, 1=recoverable, 2=critical).
API readiness probe validates control-plane token minting, route discovery, and a /healthz runtime ping within 1 minute of deployment.

Model warmup sequence successfully loads a pinned model variant, completes a 3-token generation under configured latency SLO in >=90% of attempts during smoke run, and writes an audit event to the customer's log sink.
Smoke verification runs 3 deterministic prompts covering plain text, structured JSON output, and function-call schema; failures are classified and reported.
Observed metrics and logs are visible on the private deployment dashboard with links from the deployment UI.
A runbook describing manual retry/rollback steps and escalation contacts is added to Confluence.
test_plan: Unit tests for watchdog state machine and classification logic (local).
End-to-end integration test in staging VPC that invokes the Terraform module and asserts watchdog exit codes and dashboard metrics.
Canary run in one customer sandbox VPC before rolling to broader private deploys (coordinate with Solutions Eng).
Synthetic negative test: simulate model load failure by injecting corrupt model path; verify classification and rollback suggestion.
runbook: 1) Check pipeline logs where watchdog executed; 2) Identify failure category from structured output (CONFIG / AUTH / MODEL / NETWORK / RUNTIME); 3) For CONFIG/AUTH: patch Terraform variables and re-run watchdog; 4) For MODEL: attempt a single model reload via control-plane debug endpoint, if that fails escalate to infra-oncall and open ENG-ModelLoad; 5) For NETWORK: check VPC peering and customer route table; 6) If repeated critical failures, trigger rollback to previous stable image and notify PM/SE team.
implementation_notes: - The watchdog is implemented as a small Go binary with pluggable checks. - Use existing runtime health endpoint (/internal/ready) and authenticated /v1/generate with a short prompt. - Add Terraform hooks: module outputs a 'watchdog_trigger_url' and an optional 'watchdog_token' secret resource; CI will POST to this URL to start the check. - Use exponential backoff with jitter for model load retries (max 3 attempts, 20s initial). - For Private deployments, write audit events to the customer log sink using structured JSON lines and to internal S3 bucket for incident replay.
security_considerations: Watchdog will require a short-lived token generated by the control plane; tokens must be stored in the deployment runner only and never persisted in Terraform state. Access pattern should be audited. The warmup prompt must not include customer PII. Security review required: yes. We will run threat model for remote-exec and restrict network egress for the watchdog job.
updates: 2026-03-10: RFC posted in Confluence, initial design reviewed by Runtime and Infra teams. Decisions: Go binary for portability, expose simple trigger endpoint.
2026-03-11: Added Terraform module hook implementation plan. Diego to prototype the trigger_url/secret output.

2026-03-12: Prototype run in staging completed; API readiness and simple warmup passed but observed sporadic 503s during model load — increased model load retry window and added jitter. Added ENG-37242 to follow up on transient 503 rate-limiting behavior.
2026-03-14: PR opened for watchdog binary and Terraform changes (see links). Requesting review from @marta.novak for security and @ryan.cho for runtime compatibility.
reviews_and_feedback: Marta Novak (Security): ensure tokens are ephemeral and not stored in TF state; suggested HSM-backed signing for trigger tokens. -> Action: implement short-lived signed JWTs (task assigned).

Ryan Cho (Runtime): asked to validate that the warmup path does not evict KV cache for hot requests; suggested tagging warmup requests with low-priority QoS. -> Action: add QoS header to warmup calls.
follow_up_tasks: Coordinate with Solutions Eng for sandbox canary (SE-ops contact: Priya Shah).
notes_for_QA: QA should validate exit-code semantics, check alert routing, and verify that audit events appear in both customer sink and internal replay bucket. Provide test vectors for structured-output smoke cases and ensure deterministic expected tokens for stable assertions.
deployment_instructions: - After merging the PR, bump the Terraform module version in the private-deploy pipeline. - The pipeline will fetch the watchdog binary artifact from CI and invoke the trigger endpoint. - Observe the Grafana dashboard for 'postdeploy.watchdog.*' metrics. - If smoke fails, follow the runbook to retry or rollback.
estimated_cost_impact: Low to moderate: short warmups increase egress and GPU init time per deployment; recommend adding a soft cap on warmup attempts and an opt-out flag for extremely large models.
